US-05.3 and US-06.1 say every employee subject to source tax must answer the denomination and children questions, and Liechtenstein residents count as subject. But the AC-05.7.3 examples show '–' for denomination, children and spouse employment when a Liechtenstein resident returns home daily or has at most 45 non-return days. In that case the result is 'in principle no source tax liability' and needs no tariff inputs. Should Liechtenstein residents with that outcome skip the tariff questions? If so, the Liechtenstein cross-border questions have to come before denomination, spouse employment and children in the flow. Today all of these sit together in step 6.

Many new employees move around their start date. Should they enter their current home address, or the address that will apply from the first working day? Someone moving from Germany to Zurich would get a different liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff depending on the answer. And what about weekly residents who keep a Swiss address but have their main residence abroad?

Does the employee see any of the derived results before or after submitting? These are the insurance start date, whether they are subject to source tax, and the tariff code or Liechtenstein result. The spec only says results are 'recorded for HR'. Showing them (or not) changes the closing and summary screens.

Does the employee type in a blank first working day, or does HR give a pre-filled date (e.g. from the contract) that the employee confirms or corrects? 'Enter and confirm' can be read either way. A pre-filled date needs HR input before the questionnaire starts.

The evidence for the H tariff (F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b) says a child counts with H only when it lives in the employee's household. Row 22 of the child result table, which is not marked inferred, gives 'counts with H' for a minor child outside the household (single parent with custody, alternating care, employee pays more). Which is correct? The answer changes A vs H in the tariff code.

"the employee is asked for their first working day at Muster AG as a date (DD.MM.YYYY)" - The DD.MM.YYYY format comes from the fund's date-of-birth and insurance-start-date fields and from G-10, which sets the wording used in the spec's examples. No stakeholder asks for the first working day to be typed in this format. How the date is entered is a UI decision.

"the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child" - This copies the calculator's add/remove child buttons as an interaction pattern. The business need is only that every child can be described. How several children are entered is a UI decision.

"Notes | Flow step 1 (personal details)." - The Notes rows fix a step number for each question (step 1 personal, 2 address, 3 employment, 4 residence status, 5 family, 6 source tax). This is screen sequencing beyond the business dependencies, and it limits the reordering that conditional skipping needs, for example for Liechtenstein.

info.message: What is recorded as 'Subject to source tax' for a Liechtenstein resident who gets 'in principle no source tax liability'? Is it 'yes' (lives abroad), 'no', or a third status? Does the recorded liability differ from what the US-05.7 result table shows?
Which first working days are valid? Can the date be in the past, or lie very far in the future? Must it be a weekday? The spec only requires a date.

On what date is a child's status (minor, or of age and in first education) judged: the day the questionnaire is filled in, the first working day, or the start of the tax year? This matters for a child who turns 18 around the start date.

For married employees and registered partners the children question includes the spouse's children. For such a stepchild, the custody, 'other parent' and maintenance questions are worded for the employee's own child. Should the wording change for stepchildren, or should those questions be answered from the spouse's point of view?

'HR words the reminder': is this a fixed text HR gives us once, or must HR be able to edit it themselves (per customer company, over time)? HR editing it would need a content setting that does not exist in the employee-side scope.

D-036 says inapplicable answers 'may be kept' until submission, but AC-08.2.1 requires them to come back when the earlier answer is switched back. Is keeping them mandatory? Should progress also survive closing the questionnaire and coming back later (save and resume)? Nothing is said about a partly completed questionnaire across sessions.
Every address part is required, but some valid postal addresses have no house number, such as rural addresses or named buildings. Should the questionnaire accept an address without a house number?

The AC-01.2.1 example table gives '–' for the country of a Swiss resident but 'required' for a German resident, although the text says country is always required. AC-01.3.2 mixes '–' and 'not asked' for the canton in the same way. Do '–' and 'not asked' mean the same thing in these tables, so the examples can be used as test cases?
Should first and last name be the official names as on the ID document, including all first names? Or is the name the employee normally uses enough for the pension fund registration?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: What does Pensionskasse Muster expect in 'Canton' for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and lists only Swiss cantons; employees abroad cannot be registered without an answer.
options: Canton of work (Zurich) for employees abroad
Canton of residence; the fund gives a rule for employees abroad
Canton means work canton for everyone
open_questions.recommendation: Provisionally ask only residents of Switzerland (D-002); verify with a domain expert and the fund.

open_questions.question: How does the pension fund want registered partnerships and separated employees registered (the list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), and does it want partner details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A wrong civil status or a missing partner date of birth makes the registration wrong.
options: Keep provisional mapping (both as Married with spouse/partner date of birth)
open_questions.recommendation: Use the provisional mapping (D-003) until a domain expert verifies it.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's screen ask for a spouse's date of birth (or other data) for Divorced or Widowed?

options: Extra field shown - add a question

options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live

questions.question: US-05.3 and US-06.1 say every employee subject to source tax must answer the denomination and children questions, and Liechtenstein residents count as subject. But the AC-05.7.3 examples show '–' for denomination, children and spouse employment when a Liechtenstein resident returns home daily or has at most 45 non-return days. In that case the result is 'in principle no source tax liability' and needs no tariff inputs. Should Liechtenstein residents with that outcome skip the tariff questions? If so, the Liechtenstein cross-border questions have to come before denomination, spouse employment and children in the flow. Today all of these sit together in step 6.

What is recorded as 'Subject to source tax' for a Liechtenstein resident who gets 'in principle no source tax liability'? Is it 'yes' (lives abroad), 'no', or a third status? Does the recorded liability differ from what the US-05.7 result table shows?

Many new employees move around their start date. Should they enter their current home address, or the address that will apply from the first working day? Someone moving from Germany to Zurich would get a different liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff depending on the answer. And what about weekly residents who keep a Swiss address but have their main residence abroad?

Does the employee see any of the derived results before or after submitting? These are the insurance start date, whether they are subject to source tax, and the tariff code or Liechtenstein result. The spec only says results are 'recorded for HR'. Showing them (or not) changes the closing and summary screens.

Does the employee type in a blank first working day, or does HR give a pre-filled date (e.g. from the contract) that the employee confirms or corrects? 'Enter and confirm' can be read either way. A pre-filled date needs HR input before the questionnaire starts.
Which first working days are valid? Can the date be in the past, or lie very far in the future? Must it be a weekday? The spec only requires a date.

The evidence for the H tariff (F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b) says a child counts with H only when it lives in the employee's household. Row 22 of the child result table, which is not marked inferred, gives 'counts with H' for a minor child outside the household (single parent with custody, alternating care, employee pays more). Which is correct? The answer changes A vs H in the tariff code.

On what date is a child's status (minor, or of age and in first education) judged: the day the questionnaire is filled in, the first working day, or the start of the tax year? This matters for a child who turns 18 around the start date.

For married employees and registered partners the children question includes the spouse's children. For such a stepchild, the custody, 'other parent' and maintenance questions are worded for the employee's own child. Should the wording change for stepchildren, or should those questions be answered from the spouse's point of view?

'HR words the reminder': is this a fixed text HR gives us once, or must HR be able to edit it themselves (per customer company, over time)? HR editing it would need a content setting that does not exist in the employee-side scope.

D-036 says inapplicable answers 'may be kept' until submission, but AC-08.2.1 requires them to come back when the earlier answer is switched back. Is keeping them mandatory? Should progress also survive closing the questionnaire and coming back later (save and resume)? Nothing is said about a partly completed questionnaire across sessions.
Every address part is required, but some valid postal addresses have no house number, such as rural addresses or named buildings. Should the questionnaire accept an address without a house number?

The AC-01.2.1 example table gives '–' for the country of a Swiss resident but 'required' for a German resident, although the text says country is always required. AC-01.3.2 mixes '–' and 'not asked' for the canton in the same way. Do '–' and 'not asked' mean the same thing in these tables, so the examples can be used as test cases?
Should first and last name be the official names as on the ID document, including all first names? Or is the name the employee normally uses enough for the pension fund registration?

tech_leaks.quote: the employee is asked for their first working day at Muster AG as a date (DD.MM.YYYY)
tech_leaks.why: The DD.MM.YYYY format comes from the fund's date-of-birth and insurance-start-date fields and from G-10, which sets the wording used in the spec's examples. No stakeholder asks for the first working day to be typed in this format. How the date is entered is a UI decision.

tech_leaks.quote: the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child
tech_leaks.why: This copies the calculator's add/remove child buttons as an interaction pattern. The business need is only that every child can be described. How several children are entered is a UI decision.

The Notes rows fix a step number for each question (step 1 personal, 2 address, 3 employment, 4 residence status, 5 family, 6 source tax). This is screen sequencing beyond the business dependencies, and it limits the reordering that conditional skipping needs, for example for Liechtenstein.

review.summary: No mechanical errors, all 200+ examples pass, and none of the 4 open questions is marked blocking. It is still not ready, for four reasons. (1) The child result table contradicts its own evidence on a row that is not marked inferred, so the tariff code can come out wrong (A vs H). (2) The spec is inconsistent about which tariff questions Liechtenstein residents answer, and the fixed step order leaks into the spec. (3) Several rule rows cite facts the rule does not include in its cited set. (4) Four major refinement questions are open: address timing, pre-filled start date, whether employees see results, and the Liechtenstein flow. All of these are small fixes. Once they are settled, the package should move to ready_with_caveats, with the four non-blocking open questions and the inferred child paths verified before go-live.

findings.title: Row 22 of the child result table contradicts its evidence (H vs A)
findings.why: Row 22 is not marked inferred, yet it counts a minor child outside the household with H. The cited evidence says H applies only to a child in the employee's household. Wrong tariff letter means wrong source tax deduction.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on feature.md; F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b; rule.child_tariff_result; AC-06.2.5 / AC-06.3.3
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml whether the H tariff needs the child in the household. Correct row 22 or mark it inferred, and add the path to the expert check in OQ-calculator-coverage.

findings.title: Liechtenstein flow is inconsistent: tariff questions are required but the examples skip them
findings.why: US-05.3 and US-06.1 make the denomination and children questions mandatory for everyone subject to source tax. AC-05.7.3 shows them as '–' when a Liechtenstein resident gets 'in principle no source tax liability'. Developers cannot build both, and what gets recorded as liability is unclear.
findings.action: Decide whether a Liechtenstein resident with daily return or ≤45 non-return days skips the tariff questions. Decide what 'Subject to source tax' records for them (yes / no / a third status). Ask the Liechtenstein cross-border questions before the tariff questions.

findings.title: Fixed step numbers in feature.md (technical leak)
findings.why: The Notes rows fix the screen order (steps 1–6). This is UI sequencing, and it blocks the reordering the Liechtenstein decision needs.
findings.evidence: tech_leak feature.md 'Flow step 1 (personal details)'; trace_judge story.US-01.2 (address-after-personal ordering not backed)
findings.action: Remove the step numbers. Keep only the business dependencies, i.e. which answer must be known before which question is asked.

findings.title: Rule rows cite facts that are not in the rule's cited set
findings.why: Some rows are not backed by the cited set, which weakens the audit trail for the computed liability and tariff.
findings.evidence: trace_judge rule.source_tax_result (F-hr_transcript-b6d9b3), rule.cross_border_tariff_applies (bc1639, 52b67a), rule.single_parent_h_tariff (c78e0c), rule.source_tax_residence (Germany/Liechtenstein questions), rule.pension_fund_civil_status (D-004 Separated row), item.address_country (D-002); stories US-04.3, US-05.4, US-06.1, US-08.1 (Tomás/d7431e)
findings.action: Add the missing facts and decisions to each rule's, item's or story's citations. Fix the Separated row in rule.pension_fund_civil_status: D-003 says 'without a spouse's date of birth' (it also conflicts with OQ-civil-status-partnership option 1).

findings.title: Which address counts when the employee moves around the start date?
findings.why: Liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff all depend on the home country. Someone moving from Germany to Zurich gets a different result depending on which address they enter. Weekly residents (Swiss address, main residence abroad) are not covered.
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml whether the employee enters the current address or the address that applies from the first working day, and how weekly residents are handled. Check with HR (Anna) or a domain expert.

findings.title: Does the employee type the first working day or confirm one HR pre-filled? Which dates are valid?
findings.why: A pre-filled date needs HR input before the questionnaire starts. The date drives the insurance start date.
findings.action: Decide who supplies the date (employee or HR). Set the valid range: past dates, how far ahead, weekdays only.

findings.title: Does the employee see the derived results?
findings.why: Showing or hiding the insurance start date, the liability and the tariff code changes the closing and summary screens.
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml whether the employee sees the results (insurance start date, liability, tariff) or only HR does.

findings.title: Many child-result paths are inferred, and the H-tariff purpose of child items has no backing
findings.why: Lonio now owns the tariff result. The unobserved paths and the H-tariff purpose rest on inference, not on a source.
findings.evidence: inferred_items US-06.2/06.3/06.5/06.6, rule.child_tariff_result; trace_judge item.has_children, child_* items (H-tariff purpose); trace_judge story.US-06.4 (divorced/widowed grouping); OQ-calculator-coverage
findings.action: Keep D-009 as a go-live condition. Cite an H-tariff fact (e.g. 96658b) on the child items. Have a domain expert run the inferred rows and the divorced/widowed grouping through the calculator.

findings.title: UI leaks in the stories
findings.why: The stories fix the date format and the add/remove-child pattern. Those are UI decisions, not business rules.
